- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 2+ consecutive days) and news volume is high, model tends to overreact — cap forecast peak at 1.5–2x recent high to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative sharply (e.g., -0.67+ change) or news volume drops, model often underreacts — adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% of recent range to avoid lag.  
- After a spike in price (e.g., >+1.5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- If sentiment is flat (±0.33) for 3+ days, model tends to drift — apply mean reversion: forecast = prior 7-day avg ± 0.2% of range.  
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.67+ change daily), model overfits noise — use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast.  
- If true outcome is consistently 0.5–1.0% below model (e.g., 81.5 vs 82.0), model is biased high — subtract 0.3–0.5% from forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If true outcome is consistently 0.5–1.0% above model (e.g., 81.5 vs 81.0), model is biased low — add 0.3–0.5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses 1–2-day lag — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead by +0.2–0.5% if sentiment is trending up.  
- If sentiment is rising but news volume is low, model underestimates — add 0.1–0.3% to forecast to compensate for low signal.  
- If sentiment is falling but news volume is high, model overestimates — subtract 0.1–0.3% to avoid overcorrection.
